newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish Imatran Voima sees higher 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Finnish Imatran Voima sees higher 1996 profit.

text.p: Finnish state-owned power producer Imatran Voima Oy -- due to be partly privatised next year -- said in a statement on Thursday it expected its 1996 profit would be better than in 1995.

"Kalevi Numminen, IVO's president, considers the profit trend to be fairly good and believes that good profits can be expected for the rest of the year, while the result for the full year is forecast to improve on the previous year," IVO said.
IVO reported a 1.16 billion markka January-August profit, more than double the 537 million in the corresponding period in 1995. Its full-year 1995 profit was 1.13 billion.
IVO said its volume rose a third due to Swedish electricity sales and acquisitions, most notably its merger with Gullspangs Kraft.
All units improved net sales and profits with the greatest increase in the group's main division, Power and Heat, which accounted for 57 percent of group growth, it said.
"IVO's gross investments, 3.5 billion markka, have increased signficantly in 1996. The greatest single investment was the acquisition of shares of (Swedish) Gullspangs Kraft," it said.
IVO paid 2.8 billion markka for the shares.
IVO also bought shares in Finnish electricity distrubutors, most significantly increasing its stake in Lansivoima Oy to 28.3 percent from 9.8 percent.
In addition Gullspangs in July acquired another Swedish company Ab Skandinaviska Elverk but this deal was not included in IVO's January-August financial statements.

In the period, IVO sold 75 percent of its telecommunications company Telivo to Swedish Telia for an undisclosed sum, but its equity to assets ratio fell two percentage points to 45 percent as a result of the acquisitions.
IVO estimated that this ratio would have been impaired by some seven percentage points more if Skandinaviska Elverk had been included in the result.
"Return on capital employed would have been about two percentage points lower (than the 15 percent reported)," it added.

While acquisitions boosted most IVO's units, the energy measurement business was helped by anticipation of deregulation of electricity markets, with the most significant growth in Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden, IVO said.
